chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who sleeps and does not perceive in his sleep that he has had a seminal emission, but finds water in his garment and on his thigh. Is there a ritual bath upon him? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes.

key_terms.احْتَلَمَ: To have a seminal emission (wet dream)

ai.seo_question: Is ghusl required if one wakes up with signs of seminal discharge but did not feel it during sleep?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the presence of seminal fluid (*mani*) on the body or clothing serves as objective proof of *janabah*, rendering the ritual bath (*ghusl*) obligatory even if the sleeper did not consciously perceive the emission. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that physical evidence supersedes subjective sensation in matters of ritual purity, ensuring the validity of subsequent prayers. The hadith is foundational in distinguishing between mere sleep and the state of major impurity, emphasizing the necessity of *ghusl* before engaging in acts of worship.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man who sleeps and does not sense in his sleep that he has bed-wet, but he finds the water to be in his clothes and upon his thigh, is there a washing upon him?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sama‘ah who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who does not experience any wet dream but he finds wet spots on his thigh and his clothes. Is Ghusl (bath) necessary for him? He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, Ghusl (bath) is necessary.”
